name: Colton Reed · diagnostic

biography.name: Colton Reed · diagnostic

background.family: Lives with his father and grandmother; his mother lives elsewhere and calls irregularly.
background.finances: Basic expenses are usually covered, but unexpected repairs consume savings. He has a small amount from weekend chores.
background.geography: Outside a small town near Childress in the Texas Panhandle.
background.cultureLanguages: English-speaking extended family with strong local ties and frequent teasing that he does not always enjoy.
background.school: Small public high school; several activities share one afternoon bus.
background.accessOpportunities: Neither parent attended college. His grandmother keeps school paperwork organized. Colton has an unnamed attention-related condition and describes losing track of materials even for activities he wants to do.

timeline.story: Colton wanted to carry a flashlight during every evening walk with his grandmother, even before dark. He collected smooth stones and abandoned them in coat pockets. At home he enjoyed cooking scrambled eggs with help but refused to taste the tomatoes his father kept offering him.

He and a friend swapped trading cards at recess, arguing about bent corners and whether a shiny card was really rare. Colton sometimes accepted a trade too quickly and regretted it later. He also loved a classroom singing game despite insisting at home that singing was embarrassing.

His father brought home a box of secondhand sports equipment. Colton cleaned several items and compared them with pictures in store flyers. He was disappointed that a carefully scrubbed glove still smelled musty. He played baseball that spring, then became more interested in bicycling with two neighbors.

For a school project he compared the price and quantity of several packages of seeds. He liked noticing that the largest package was not always cheapest per packet. The presentation arrived a day late because he left it on the kitchen table, a problem his good calculations did not solve.

He tried selling a few cleaned secondhand game accessories to people his family knew. One item did not work consistently, and refunding the buyer used most of what he had earned. He disliked admitting the mistake and avoided another sale for months, while continuing to browse listings for fun.

Colton compared three offers for supplies used at a school booth, including delivery costs that a friend initially ignored. He also underestimated how many boxes they could carry. His an unnamed attention-related condition was already known at school; a checklist helped with some handoffs, but he still forgot it when rushing.

He is experimenting with occasional resale of used board games, checking missing pieces at the kitchen table. He enjoys comparing what different sellers include and is less interested in photographing each box. A recent game has attracted no buyers. He alternates between lowering its price and deciding he might keep it.

biography.selfDescription: Comparing stuff is interesting. Posting it and waiting for answers is mostly annoying. People act like those are the same activity.
openQuestions: Will he keep wanting to do the less interesting parts?
How much financial uncertainty can he tolerate without withdrawing?
variationTags: an unnamed attention-related condition independently stated

response.branchReason: Comparing full offers, package quantities, and resale prices is a repeated voluntary interest. A budget is a small extension; investment analysis and sustained business management are still untested. Branch omissions preserve that limit.
response.financialAssumptions: A dependable used vehicle and a trial in a larger town support a modest rented place, used car, and savings room. Other spending levels are tentative ordinary preferences, not deductions from household income. No education route is ruled out by access or organization difficulties.

responseRationales.evidence: Cleaning used gear and testing accessories show attention to objects, but he does not express a wish to build cabinets, lay tile, assemble electronics, or make repairs; these remain unsure.

Seed package work was about prices rather than growing or studying organisms. Stones and evening walks do not establish laboratory, environmental, astronomy, fire investigation, or firefighting interests; all remain unsure.

He explicitly dislikes photographing and describing resale items, supporting mild dislike of related editing work, but has not rejected writing stories, drawing, effects, or set painting. Those unfamiliar creative tasks remain unsure.

He enjoyed a childhood singing game while finding singing embarrassing at home. This mixed and old evidence does not establish either current enthusiasm or aversion to instruments, composing, dance, or band singing.

Bicycling and board games are leisure preferences, without evidence of wanting to teach exercise, sports, a class, sign language, or provide personal care and counseling. Helping activities remain unsure.

Card exchanges and repeated small resale experiments support liking buying/selling, negotiating, starting a small venture, and merchandise sales. Managing stores or departments is untested. Clothing marketing resembles the posting he finds annoying; law and salon operations remain unsure.

He enjoys comparing quantities and checking that used items work, supporting calculator use and quality testing. Spreadsheets, network installation, and delivery driving are unfamiliar; wanting a vehicle is not evidence of enjoying deliveries.

He explicitly loses interest in repetitive follow-through and dislikes long repetitive assignments, supporting mild dislike of sustained inventory and mail sorting. Proofreading forms, payroll, shipping logs, and rent records are not described and remain unsure.

Income needed for your choices $70K–$85K / year Before tax. The lower end covers your costs. The upper end adds a cushion.
The car also needs $4,000 down. This is separate from the monthly total.
More info · how we add it up

Everyday essentials cover phone, home supplies, health, and any saved debt or care costs. These are editable estimates, not price quotes. Home and car purchases also take upfront money. Phone, household, and health costs are included; existing debt and care needs are kept. The income range estimates 2026 employee taxes and retirement saving, then adds room to leave 20% of take-home unallocated at the upper end. It is a budget target range, not an income ceiling or a probability.

lifestyleSummaryText: YOUR AUSTIN PICTURE Here’s how your choices add up.
One adult. Monthly planning amounts, rounded to keep it simple.
Includes cash savings and everyday essentials.
Income needed for your choices $70K–$85K / year Before tax. The lower end covers your costs. The upper end adds a cushion.
The car also needs $4,000 down. This is separate from the monthly total.
More info · how we add it up

Everyday essentials cover phone, home supplies, health, and any saved debt or care costs. These are editable estimates, not price quotes. Home and car purchases also take upfront money. Phone, household, and health costs are included; existing debt and care needs are kept. The income range estimates 2026 employee taxes and retirement saving, then adds room to leave 20% of take-home unallocated at the upper end. It is a budget target range, not an income ceiling or a probability.
